name: GlassSearchField
material_impl: Thin wrapper over GlassInput (shared). No material of its own; clear button is GlassButton ghost/sm. Inherits whatever GlassInput renders.
a11y: type=search plus a redundant role=searchbox. Default label 'Search'. Icon is aria-hidden. Clear button has aria-label. The clear button only renders when the field is controlled AND onClear is passed; uncontrolled usage (the 'Empty' story) never shows a clear affordance. GlassSearchField sets its own clearable=true default but does not forward it, so GlassInput's built-in clear button is bypassed.
api: forwardRef to HTMLInputElement and extends GlassInputProps, so it gets className/style passthrough. Clear behaviour is controlled-only. No Escape-to-clear and no onSearch/submit semantics.
fake_complexity: None. It is honest and small.
target: LiquidGlassSearchField (single search field), or make it a documented preset of GlassInput
justification: This is a reasonable 60-line preset, but the library ships two root-exported search fields (GlassSearchField and LiquidGlassSearchField) plus GlassIntelligentSearch. The clear button only works when the field is controlled and onClear is passed, and the role is redundant. Keep one search field as the canonical one. Implement clear internally for uncontrolled usage, add Escape-to-clear, and forward clearable correctly. No certification screenshot exists for it.

name: GlassSelect (legacy, options-array)
tests: src/components/input/GlassSelect.test.tsx (8 boilerplate tests: smoke, axe on empty select, snapshot; none open the menu or select an option)
material_impl: Mixed. The trigger is GlassButton with ~15 ad-hoc classes (glass-surface-dark/20, glass-border-white/20, glass-backdrop-blur-sm). Non-default variants wrap it in OptimizedGlass. The dropdown is OptimizedGlass plus raw Tailwind (shadow-2xl shadow-black/50, ring-white/10, bg-white/20). The repo has no Tailwind compiler, so many classes (h-10, rotate-180, bg-white/15, border-destructive/50) resolve to nothing. The intensity/depth/tint/border/animation props passed to OptimizedGlass are discarded by OptimizedGlassCore. The variantClasses and stateClasses maps are defined but never applied. The chevron and checkmark are the text glyphs '▼' and '✓'.
motion: Motion preset slideDown, reduced-motion aware via MotionFramer. The chevron rotation uses the non-existent rotate-180 class. useReducedMotion and ANIMATION are imported but unused.
a11y: Serious defects. (1) A visually hidden native <select> stays focusable alongside the trigger button, giving two tab stops and duplicate labels. (2) Options have no ids and there is no aria-activedescendant, so arrow-key 'focus' is visual only. (3) The FocusTrap wraps a list with no focusable items unless searchable is set. (4) The document mousedown outside-handler checks only triggerRef. The listbox is portalled outside the trigger, so mousedown on an option should close the menu before click fires. Mouse selection is likely broken; verify in a real browser. (5) The trigger lacks role=combobox, aria-controls and aria-activedescendant. (6) The helper/error text is not linked via aria-describedby.
api: forwardRef targets the hidden <select>, which is not the interactive element. Controlled-only: there is no defaultValue path, and the custom UI never fires native onChange, so onChange users get nothing. ...props (including the non-DOM 'label') is spread onto the <select>. className is applied twice (outer and inner wrapper). Marked @deprecated in favour of a 'Radix-based compound Select', but the compound is not Radix-based.
ssr: 'use client'. createPortal targets document.body after a mount flag. OK.
fake_complexity: Claims searchable/multi/grouping/validation states. Search and grouping work. State styling and variant styling are dead maps. 'Radix-based' replacement claim is false.
target: GlassSelectCompound (after it is rebuilt on a real listbox/combobox primitive)
justification: The legacy select is already self-declared deprecated, yet it holds the root `GlassSelect` name. It has broken focus semantics (a duplicate hidden select), mouse selection likely broken by its outside-click handler, controlled-only state, dead variant/state maps, and text-glyph chevrons. Tests never open it. It should become a thin adapter over the compound select, with options mapped to Item children, for one major version, and then be removed. The certification screenshot could not be visually inspected in this run (the image reader returned nothing). Certification marked it 'passed' after inspecting only the storybook-default-dark theme.

name: GlassSelectCompound (GlassSelectRoot/Trigger/Content/Item/Value/Label/Group/Separator/ScrollUp/ScrollDown)
material_impl: Bespoke. Uses no OptimizedGlass/LiquidGlass. The content uses raw 'glass-backdrop-blur-lg bg-white/10 ring-1 ring-white/15 shadow-2xl shadow-black/40' plus tailwindcss-animate classes (animate-in, zoom-in-95, slide-in-from-top-2). Those animate classes do not exist in this repo, which has no Tailwind compiler. The trigger uses glass-surface-subtle/10 and focus:ring-primary. The error state is hard-coded border-red-400 (undefined class). The material does not match the rest of the library.
motion: Motion preset scaleIn (reduced-motion aware). The tailwind-animate data-state classes are dead.
a11y: Better skeleton than the legacy select: role=combobox, aria-expanded/controls, role=listbox/option, aria-selected, typeahead on the trigger. Gaps: (1) no arrow-key navigation inside the listbox. Items are tabIndex -1, focus never moves into content, data-highlighted is never set, and Home/End are absent. (2) The trigger hard-codes aria-label='Select option', which overrides the visible GlassSelectValue text and any external <label>. (3) ScrollUp/ScrollDown 'buttons' always render, are aria-hidden and do nothing. (4) DismissableLayer dismisses on pointerdown on the trigger, then the trigger click toggles open again, so clicking the trigger to close it re-opens the menu. (5) Escape does not restore focus to the trigger. (6) Items register labels only when content is mounted, so typeahead and defaultValue labels do not work until the menu has been opened once.
api: Clean Radix-like API shape with controlled/uncontrolled value and open state, name with a hidden input, and forwardRef on parts. But the root export naming is confusing: `GlassSelect` (root) is the legacy component, while this one is `GlassSelectRoot`/`GlassSelectCompound`, and the file-internal name is also GlassSelect. position/variant props are accepted and ignored (variant: _variant).
ssr: 'use client'. The Portal primitive is used. Fine.
fake_complexity: The doc comment in the legacy file calls it 'Radix-based'. It is hand-rolled. The scroll buttons are decorative fakes.
target: Canonical AuraGlass 5 Select built on primitives/roving-focus + positioning, with a shared Liquid material listbox surface
justification: The compound API is the right shape and is the obvious foundation for the single 5.0 select. The internals are not production grade: no in-list keyboard navigation, an anchor-dismiss toggle bug, a hard-coded aria-label, dead scroll buttons, and dead Tailwind animation classes. Its material does not use the library's own glass primitive. A premium select is a flagship surface in any glass system (Apple's pop-up menus are its most recognisable 'material' moment). Rebuild it on RovingFocusGroup/Positioner, render content through LiquidGlassMaterial, and make it the only select with legacy GlassSelect as an adapter. Screenshot not viewable in this run.

name: GlassSlider
tests: src/components/input/GlassSlider.test.tsx (10 tests, boilerplate; no keyboard or drag tests)
material_impl: The thumb is OptimizedGlass (level3, border='glow', animation='float') with an inline background var(--glass-neutral-level3-surface). OptimizedGlassCore discards animation/intensity/depth/tint/border, so 'float' and 'glow' are no-ops. The track uses glass-surface-subtle and the fill uses glass-surface-{primary|success|danger}. The fill has a 'glass-sheen' overlay class that is not defined in any CSS. The background div repeats glass-gradient-primary three times, with a garbled class list. The 'warning' and 'info' variants reuse the primary border and info reuses the primary fill.
motion: The fill has an inline 'transition: all 150ms ease' that is not reduced-motion gated. useMotionPreferenceContext gates only the no-op float. glass-scale-110 is applied on drag.
a11y: Critical: role=slider thumbs have tabIndex=0 but no onKeyDown handler at all, so there is no Arrow/PageUp/Home/End support. Keyboard users cannot operate the slider. There is no aria-orientation. aria-label and aria-labelledby are both set, and range thumbs share the same label. announceToScreenReader fires on every pointermove, flooding screen readers. A 20px thumb is below 24/44px touch targets. The <label htmlFor> points to a div, not a labelable element.
api: forwardRef on the container. value/defaultValue are fine. onChange and onValueChange fire identically. onValueCommit uses the stale valueArray captured at pointerdown, so it commits the value from before the drag. useA11yId is called conditionally (label ? useA11yId(...) : undefined), a Rules of Hooks violation that breaks when label/description/error toggle. material, neutralValue, showTickLabels and interactionGlass are rendered only as data-attributes that no CSS reads (fake props). thumbContent, inverted and range exist.
ssr: 'use client'. Document listeners only in handlers. OK.
fake_complexity: material='liquid', interactionGlass, neutralValue and showTickLabels are advertised but inert. 'float' and 'glow' do nothing.
justification: A Liquid Glass slider (a refractive thumb that magnifies the track) is one of the most recognisable Liquid Glass controls and is flagship material. The current one fails basic WCAG because there is no keyboard operation at all. It also violates hook rules, commits stale values, floods the live region, and advertises four inert props. Rebuild it on pointer capture with keyboard support (step/page/home/end), aria-orientation and a single debounced announcement. Use a real LiquidGlassMaterial thumb and token-driven fill, and drop the fake props. Screenshot not viewable in this run.

name: GlassStep
material_impl: OptimizedGlass (intent/elevation/tier) per step, wrapped in Motion. Hover uses 'hover:bg-glass-light-primary/5 glass-hover-scale-1-01', which are undefined/raw classes. Each step is its own glass slab, so a stepper made of these would stack N blurred surfaces.
motion: A Motion wrapper with no preset (no-op). CSS transition-all 300ms (not gated).
a11y: role=button when clickable, else role=listitem with no list parent. A verbose aria-label duplicates the visible text. aria-current=step. Keyboard Enter/Space works when clickable.
api: Internal-shaped API: requires step/index/active/completed/orientation. The local GlassStepProps interface is dead; the component uses GlassStepInternalProps from types.ts. No composition parent consumes it: interactive/GlassStepper, GlassFormStepper and GlassWizard all render their own step markup.
fake_complexity: None, but it is an orphan building block.
target: single Stepper/Steps component (interactive/GlassStepper) with Step as a composable child
justification: This is an internal step cell that nothing in the library composes, yet it is root-exported alongside its own icon and label sub-pieces. The library already has at least five other step-indicator implementations. Fold it into one Steps component (Steps.Root/Steps.Item) with a single shared material rail rather than per-step glass slabs, and stop exporting it standalone.

name: GlassStepIcon
material_impl: OptimizedGlass circle with state classes 'bg-primary-500 border-primary-300 shadow-[0_0_12px_3px_hsl(...)]' (active) and 'bg-success-500' (completed). These Tailwind classes are not defined in the repo's CSS (no Tailwind build), so active and completed states fall back to the neutral glass surface. Hard-coded w-6/h-6.
a11y: aria-hidden (correct as decoration). The 24px size is fine for decoration.
api: React.FC with no forwardRef. The props interface is not exported. `typeof icon === 'string' ? icon : icon` is a no-op branch.
target: internal part of consolidated Steps component
justification: This is a decorative sub-part with no consumer outside GlassStep. Its state colours depend on Tailwind classes that do not exist here, so active and completed states are visually indistinguishable unless the consumer runs Tailwind with the library in its content paths. It should not be public API.

name: GlassStepLabel
material_impl: A plain span. It imports OptimizedGlass and never uses it. Colours are hard-coded 'text-slate-950' (active) and 'text-slate-700' (completed and default are identical). These classes are not defined in repo CSS, and if Tailwind were present they would be dark-on-dark in dark themes. It accepts intent/elevation/tier and ignores them.
a11y: No semantics. Completed and upcoming states differ only by nothing (identical classes).
api: React.FC with no forwardRef. intent/elevation/tier are inert props.
fake_complexity: Glass props are accepted and ignored.
duplicates: Step label markup in interactive/GlassStepper, GlassWizard, GlassFormStepper
target: internal part of consolidated Steps component
justification: This is a span with theme-breaking hard-coded slate colours (undefined in this repo), identical completed and default states, and three ignored glass props. It has no consumer besides GlassStep. Remove it from the public surface.

name: GlassStepper (input; numeric spin button)
material_impl: The +/- buttons and input well are OptimizedGlass (animation='float', depth, tint, which are all discarded). The variant colours are raw Tailwind (border-green-200/30, bg-amber-50/30, bg-blue-50/20) that do not exist in repo CSS. Inline SVG plus/minus.
motion: The Motion scaleIn preset is gated by isMotionSafe. 'float' is a no-op. glass-hover-scale-105/active:scale-95 classes are undefined. useGlassSound plays a 'tap' sound on every increment.
a11y: Input role=spinbutton with aria-valuenow/min/max and ArrowUp/Down. Buttons are divs with role=button plus Enter/Space. Issues: touch fires both onTouchStart and the synthetic onMouseDown, giving a double increment per tap. The long-press interval re-invokes an increment closure that captured the old currentValue, so holding repeats the same value instead of accumulating. There is no PageUp/Home/End. Buttons are not disabled semantically (no aria-disabled). The outer div gets id={id} while the input gets finalId, which duplicates the id when the user passes one. Every change is announced.
api: forwardRef on the inner div. ...props is destructured but never spread, so data-*/aria-*/event props are silently dropped. The name collides with the root-exported GlassStepper (interactive/GlassStepper.tsx, a progress stepper). It is semantically a NumberField, not a stepper. Conditional useA11yId calls violate hook rules.
fake_complexity: None, but there are hidden side effects (sound).
target: new GlassNumberField (built on GlassInput + spinbutton semantics)
justification: It is not exported anywhere, so it is effectively dead code with a misleading name that collides with the public progress GlassStepper. The behaviour has concrete bugs: double increments on touch, a long-press that does not accumulate, dropped props, duplicate ids, and hook-rule violations. It also plays sounds by default. Replace it with a properly named NumberField that reuses GlassInput, and delete this file.

name: GlassSwitch
material_impl: The track is OptimizedGlass as=button, which switches elevation level1 to level2 when checked. tint='primary', intensity and animation='shimmer' are discarded by OptimizedGlassCore. The variantConfig.track colours (bg-primary, bg-green-500, ...) are never applied, so the 'success/warning/error/info' variants change nothing visible on the track. The thumb uses bg-white (defined only under [data-glass-component]) or bg-foreground/80 (undefined), so the unchecked thumb may render without fill. The thumb is positioned with px translateX and is not vertically centred (track 24, thumb 20, no align-items). Checked travel leaves a 6px right gap versus a 2px left gap.
motion: The thumb uses CSS transition-all 200ms, not gated by reduced motion. 'shimmer' is a no-op.
a11y: role=switch with aria-checked on a real button and a label htmlFor. aria-invalid/required are set, and the error role=alert. Each toggle is announced via the live region, which duplicates the native switch state announcement. No RTL support for the thumb direction. Thumb travel is not visible in high-contrast mode because state is not conveyed by colour on the track.
api: forwardRef(HTMLButtonElement). checked/defaultChecked/onChange/onCheckedChange are fine. labelPosition, icons, loading and thumbContent exist. material='liquid' is a data-attribute only. Conditional useA11yId calls violate hook rules. When label/description/error are present, className goes to the button, not the wrapper.
fake_complexity: The variant colours and material='liquid' are inert.
justification: The Liquid Glass switch (an elongating lens thumb on a tinted track) is a signature control, and this one has a sound semantic base (a real button with role=switch). Visually it cannot express state. Track variant colours are never applied, the tint is discarded by the primitive, the thumb fill may be undefined when off, and the thumb is mis-centred with asymmetric travel. Rebuild the visuals on tokens: a tinted track fill, a centred thumb computed from padding, an RTL-aware logical transform and reduced-motion gating. Use LiquidGlassMaterial for the thumb. Keep the API.

name: GlassTextarea
material_impl: Bespoke. .glass-textarea in glass.css forces background/border with !important (rgba white 0.12/0.28 plus blur-sm). This overrides all four variant maps (bg-background/50, bg-muted/50, ...) and the state border colours, so default/filled/outlined/minimal and error/warning/success all render the same. It imports OptimizedGlass and does not use it. It uses 'glass-pulse-ring', an undefined class.
motion: loading adds animate-pulse (not reduced-motion gated). The duration-[${ANIMATION.DURATION.fast}ms] template class cannot be generated without Tailwind.
a11y: Label htmlFor/id are correct. aria-invalid is set. Bug: when both helperText and errorText are set, aria-describedby points to the helper id, but the helper is not rendered in the error state, leaving a dangling reference and an unannounced error. The error text is styled glass-text-primary (not an error colour) and is not role=alert. The error icon and custom icon overlap at the same position (top-3 right-3). The required asterisk uses aria-label on a span.
api: forwardRef with a merged ref. autoResize, minRows/maxRows and showCharCount exist, but the char count and auto-resize work only when controlled (they depend on the value prop). Uncontrolled textareas never resize or count. className goes to the wrapper, not the textarea. The variant/state API is visually inert.
ssr: getComputedStyle only in an effect. Safe.
fake_complexity: Variants and states are fake because of the !important override.
justification: The core is acceptable and visually consistent, because the CSS override unifies everything. But the variant and state API is fake, error semantics are broken (dangling describedby, error not coloured or announced), auto-resize and char count ignore uncontrolled usage, and icons overlap. Fix these against GlassInput's field contract, preferably by sharing a FieldShell for label/helper/error. Remove the dead variants or make them real through tokens.

name: GlassTimeField
material_impl: GlassInput type=time plus a Clock icon. Shared material via GlassInput.
a11y: Native time input semantics, default label 'Time', icon aria-hidden. The native picker indicator is not styled for dark glass, so expect a mismatch with the browser chrome.
api: forwardRef with GlassInputProps passthrough. Honest and minimal.
justification: This is a correct, tiny preset over GlassInput with native semantics. Polish later by styling the native ::-webkit-calendar-picker-indicator for glass themes, and add a test. No certification screenshot exists.

name: GlassToggle (+ non-exported GlassToggleGroup, GlassToggleGroupItem, useToggle, useToggleGroup)
material_impl: OptimizedGlass (level1 to level3 when pressed) plus raw classes bg-white/8, bg-white/12, bg-white/15, scale-105 and glass-hover-scale-105. Most of these are undefined in repo CSS (bg-white/8 and /12 are not even standard Tailwind steps). The pressed state therefore relies only on the elevation class change. The group container is bespoke 'bg-white/5 border-white/10'. The ghost variant uses an infinite glass-animate-pulse overlay while pressed.
motion: The Motion wrapper gets framer whileHover/whileTap (reduced-motion handled by MotionFramer). The ghost pressed state pulses forever (not gated).
a11y: Broken. It renders a <div role=button> (OptimizedGlass default element) with no tabIndex and no key handler, so it is not keyboard reachable or operable. The Motion wrapper has tabIndex=-1 and pointer-events-none. 'disabled' only short-circuits the click, with no aria-disabled, and the disabled: pseudo-classes do not apply to a div. aria-pressed is present.
api: forwardRef is typed HTMLButtonElement but attaches to a div. shape is a union containing a CSS class name ('glass-radius-md'). material='liquid' is a data-attribute only. Critical group bug: GlassToggleGroupItem destructures `value` and does not forward it, so GlassToggle's `'value' in props` check is always false. The item is also controlled via `pressed` with no onPressedChange, so clicking a group item does nothing; the group's onValueChange never fires. The story uses exactly this path. GlassToggleGroup/Item are not exported from root or the input index, so they are unreachable for consumers anyway.
fake_complexity: The toggle group looks functional in the story but is inert.
target: src/components/toggle-button/ToggleButton + ToggleButtonGroup (rebuilt on a real <button> + RovingFocusGroup), rendered inside LiquidGlassControlGroup
justification: This toggle is not keyboard accessible: a div role=button with no tabIndex or key handling. Its group variant is functionally dead because `value` is dropped, and its pressed styling depends on non-existent classes. A separate toggle-button family already exists. Merge into one ToggleButton/ToggleButtonGroup on a native button with roving focus, and remove GlassToggle (or alias it) in 5.0.

name: GlassTransferList
material_impl: An outer OptimizedGlass (elevation prop). The inner lists, search inputs and buttons use raw bg-white/5, bg-white/10, hover:bg-white/5 and active:bg-white/20 (the /5 and /10 classes are defined only under [data-glass-component]). Native unstyled checkboxes. Inline SVG chevrons. A <style> tag is injected per instance for the mobile column layout.
motion: duration-[${ANIMATION.DURATION.fast}ms] template classes cannot exist without Tailwind. Effectively there is no motion.
a11y: Native checkboxes inside labels are fine. Search inputs have placeholder only and no label. The lists have no role/aria-label and no aria-labelledby to their h3 titles. Bug: TransferButton is a component defined inside render, so every state change remounts the buttons. After pressing 'Move selected' with the keyboard, focus is lost to body. Item counts are not announced.
api: forwardRef. Controlled-only (value defaults to [], no defaultValue), so it is inert without onChange. 'Move all right' ignores the active search filter. minHeight/maxHeight are strings.
ssr: Safe. The inline <style> renders server-side but duplicates per instance.
target: GlassMultiSelect (or a later rebuilt pattern in a workflows recipe)
justification: It is not exported anywhere, so it is dead to consumers. Transfer lists are an outdated enterprise pattern that conflicts with a premium glass aesthetic. The implementation loses keyboard focus on every move, has unlabeled search fields and unlabeled lists, and is controlled-only. Remove it from the component set. If needed later, rebuild it as a documented recipe composed from GlassCheckboxGroup and GlassSearchField.

name: GlassTreeSelect
material_impl: The trigger is raw 'bg-white/5 border glass-border-subtle hover:bg-white/10 ring-2 ring-blue-500/50' (hard-coded blue, undefined class). The dropdown is OptimizedGlass, absolutely positioned and not portalled, so it is clipped by overflow-hidden ancestors. The chevron rotation uses undefined rotate-90/rotate-180 classes. Native checkboxes.
a11y: Poor. There is no tree semantics (no role=tree/treeitem, aria-expanded or aria-level). Nodes are div role=button containing a nested <button> (expand) and an <input> (checkbox), which is invalid nested interactive content. The expand button has no aria-label and no aria-expanded. There is no arrow-key navigation, Escape does not close, and the trigger has no aria-haspopup/aria-expanded. The search input uses autoFocus with no label.
api: forwardRef on the wrapper. Controlled-only: value defaults to [] and onChange defaults to a no-op, so uncontrolled use is impossible. Bug: setExpandedNodes is called inside the filteredData useMemo during render, a side-effect-in-render that triggers React warnings and extra renders on every keystroke. The trigger shows labels joined by commas, with no chips or overflow handling.
target: compose canonical Select popover + tree-view/TreeView (role=tree) as a TreeSelect recipe
justification: It is unexported and lacks tree ARIA. It nests interactive elements, mutates state during render, is not portalled, and hard-codes blue. The library already has three tree implementations, one of them (tree-view/TreeView) with proper role=tree. Rebuild TreeSelect as a composition of the canonical Select popover and TreeView rather than maintaining a fourth tree.

name: GlassValidationMessage
material_impl: OptimizedGlass as='p' (level1). Tone colours are 'text-red-800', 'text-amber-900' and 'text-emerald-800'. None of these classes is defined in repo CSS (no Tailwind build), so error/warning/success render in the default text colour and are distinguishable only by icon. If Tailwind were present, the dark 800/900 shades would fail contrast on dark glass. Putting a glass slab behind every field message adds a blur layer per field.
a11y: error uses role=alert and the other tones role=status. The icon is aria-hidden. The tone is not conveyed in text (no visually hidden 'Error:' prefix), so it relies on colour, which is also missing. The id is not auto-wired to the field's aria-describedby.
api: forwardRef(HTMLParagraphElement), className passthrough, tone and icon override. Simple and clean.
duplicates: Inline error/helper text in GlassInput, GlassTextarea, GlassSelect, GlassSwitch and GlassSlider (each re-implements it)
justification: This is the right primitive and should become the single message renderer used by every field, instead of each field duplicating error markup. Replace the undefined Tailwind tone classes with semantic tokens (--glass-status-danger-fg, etc.) that meet contrast on all themes. Add a visually hidden tone prefix, and drop the glass slab by default (inline text plus icon), keeping it as an opt-in variant. No certification screenshot exists.

name: GlassWizard (+ non-exported GlassWizardStep, GlassWizardStepper, useWizard)
material_impl: Composes GlassCard, CardHeader/Content, GlassProgress and GlassButton (shared primitives, good). The step pills use raw 'bg-primary/20 text-primary-foreground border-primary/40' and 'bg-green-500/20 text-green-400', which are undefined classes, so state is conveyed only by the icon swap. The step content is forced to 'text-slate-950', which is undefined here and theme-breaking if Tailwind exists. GlassWizardStepper is entirely raw Tailwind (bg-green-500, w-10 h-10, w-12 h-0.5) and renders unstyled without Tailwind.
motion: Motion fadeIn and slideIn per step (keyed, reduced-motion aware). OK.
a11y: Step nav is a <nav> of buttons with aria-current=step, which is good. aria-label overrides the visible title. The step error is role=alert. Focus is not moved to the new step heading on navigation. Step titles are hidden below sm via 'glass-hidden sm:glass-inline', leaving number-only pills on mobile.
api: Not forwardRef. With a controlled currentStep and no onStepChange the wizard is frozen, and both stories do exactly that (currentStep: 0 / 1 without a handler). The top step nav lets users jump forward past unvalidated intermediate steps: it validates only the current step and ignores allowSkip. The useWizard fallback returns a different shape (nextStep/previousStep/totalSteps) from the real context (goToNext/goToPrevious), so the TypeScript union is inconsistent. wizardData/setData exist, but steps have no ergonomic access because step content is static ReactNode. validationMode='onChange' is effectively the same as onNext. Error messages are hard-coded English strings.
fake_complexity: Claims 'comprehensive features'. Validation is a boolean callback with a hard-coded generic error string. GlassWizardStep is a no-op div that ignores its step prop.
target: one Wizard/MultiStepForm in the ./workflows subpath, using the consolidated Steps component
justification: At least five overlapping multi-step implementations exist (GlassWizard, GlassMultiStepForm, GlassFormStepper, GlassWizardTemplate, GlassFormWizardSteps). This one composes real primitives, but its state is undermined by undefined classes. It permits skipping validation through the step nav, has a frozen controlled mode in its own stories, ships an inconsistent useWizard fallback, and has a no-op GlassWizardStep. Pick one wizard and give it step-scoped data/validation via render props or context. Move focus on step change, use token-driven step states and the shared Steps component.

name: LiquidGlassControlGroup
material_impl: Shared Liquid primitives: LiquidGlassMaterial (material='liquid', variant regular/clear, radius full) wrapping LiquidGlassEffectGroup. This is the correct material architecture. However, the story overrides the group's background, border and box-shadow with !important CSS, and the child buttons are unstyled story buttons. The certified look therefore comes from story CSS, not the component.
motion: None of its own (it depends on LiquidGlassEffectGroup).
a11y: No role=group/toolbar or aria-orientation. rovingFocus defaults to true but is only emitted as data-roving-focus. No keyboard handling exists, even though primitives/RovingFocusGroup exists in the repo. selectionMode is only data-selection-mode, with no aria-pressed/checked management.
api: forwardRef with className passthrough. orientation works (flex-col). density, selectionMode and rovingFocus are inert data-attributes that no CSS or JS reads.
fake_complexity: The rovingFocus, selectionMode and density props promise behaviour that does not exist.
justification: This is the one component in the shard that uses the intended Liquid material stack (LiquidGlassMaterial + LiquidGlassEffectGroup), and a segmented/toolbar control group is a core Liquid Glass flagship (merged lenses). But its behavioural props are fakes. Wire RovingFocusGroup, role=toolbar/radiogroup by selectionMode, aria-orientation and managed pressed/checked state, and make density real. Move the story's !important look into the component, then make it the base for ToggleButtonGroup and segmented controls. No certification screenshot exists.
